newsitem.title: USA: Marks Bros Jewelers shares fall again.
newsitem.headline: Marks Bros Jewelers shares fall again.

text.p: Shares of Marks Brothers Jewelers Inc, which plunged 37 percent Monday, slid again Friday on the possibility of disappointing Christmas sales, an analyst said.

"The early reports indicate that Christmas sales (for all retailers) were disappointing," David Lebedeff, a retail analyst at NatCity Investments Inc, said. "That (Marks Brothers stock decline) could carry forward next week as sales results are announced."

A Marks Brothers spokeswoman said none of the company's officers were available to comment on the volatile activity, which also saw at least 20 large blocks of shares change hands in Friday's session.
She added the company will report fourth quarter results next week, most likely on Thursday.
"The company's management has been in a quiet period since the beginning of the quarter," David Ricci, an analyst at William Blair & Co, said.
Ricci also said he had revised his fourth quarter earnings estimate for Marks Brothers to $0.59 per share from $0.67.

Marks Brothers shares lost 37 percent of their value Monday after Montgomery Securities Inc lowered its fourth quarter estimate to $0.57 a share from $0.66. The company has yet to respond publicly to the revision.
Lebedeff believes the fact that Marks Brothers went public in May could be at the root of the sell-off. The company will be reporting its first holiday season results as a publicly traded company.

"The environment in late 1995 and 1996 saw people fighting and punching and scratching to buy retail stocks," he said. "Now, as the December numbers begin to trickle in, people are becoming afraid of those issues. You have two classic factors at work here: greed and fear."
Marks Brothers, which operates a chain of 149 jewelry stores, traded as high as 28-1/4 after going public.
The company's shares were down 1-5/8 Friday at 10-5/8.
